items.headline: Houthi strikes hit Saudi airports and oil sites
items.summary: Houthi rebels struck Saudi airports, killing three people and wounding dozens, as Yemen's war escalates. Earlier strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure are adding to regional tension and pushing oil prices up.

items.headline: Russian strike on a Ukrainian bus kills 30
items.summary: Russian attacks in eastern Ukraine, including a strike on a public bus, killed 30 people, while power outages in Kyiv are getting worse.

items.headline: South Korea recalls its ambassador to Ukraine and tests a hypersonic weapon
items.summary: Seoul is pulling its ambassador from Kyiv over a dispute about North Korean prisoners of war. Separately, South Korea flight-tested its first homegrown hypersonic weapon after a North Korean hypersonic launch and mine blasts that wounded three South Korean soldiers.

items.headline: Isaias becomes a hurricane as the Gulf Coast prepares
items.summary: Isaias has strengthened into a hurricane, and Gulf Coast residents are preparing for storms. Forecasters had said a week ago that the Atlantic might go the whole season without a hurricane.

items.headline: Midterms: about 60 House seats will decide control, and Kansas is now a Senate battleground
items.summary: Both parties are concentrating money on roughly 60 House districts that Trump carried by about nine points on average in 2024. In Kansas, Republican Sen. Roger Marshall faces a tightening race against Democrat Adam Hamilton.

items.headline: Trump's $90 Medicare rebate rolls out, but millions don't qualify
items.summary: The administration is sending one-time $90 payments toward Medicare Part B premiums at an estimated cost of $2 billion. Many enrollees aren't eligible, and critics call it a political stunt ahead of the midterms.

items.headline: ICE quietly used a New Jersey warehouse as a detention site, neighbors say
items.summary: An NPR investigation examines local accounts that ICE ran a detention facility out of a warehouse in Roxbury, New Jersey, over the summer. The report raises questions about oversight of temporary detention sites.

items.headline: A $110 billion Skydance deal for Warner Bros. Discovery
items.summary: The Ellison family's proposed purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, owner of CNN and the Warner studio, would concentrate control over major news and entertainment outlets. Critics argue it would leave less room for dissent.

items.headline: Crypto and prediction markets grow while their regulator shrinks
items.summary: The CFTC has to write new rules for crypto and prediction markets, but its staff and enforcement have dropped sharply under the second Trump administration.

items.headline: French students invoke May 1968 in school-funding protests
items.summary: Students protesting underfunded schools in France are carrying signs that reference the 1968 uprising, which nearly brought down the government.

digest.overview:
At home, Hurricane Isaias has strengthened and the Gulf Coast is preparing for landfall, with the storm already complicating plans for this weekend's Georgia-Alabama football game. In politics, both parties are pouring money into about 60 competitive House districts, and Kansas has become an unexpected Senate battleground. In business, the Ellison family's $110 billion Skydance bid for Warner Bros. Discovery is drawing media-concentration concerns, and the regulator for crypto and prediction markets is shrinking as those markets grow. The administration's one-time $90 Medicare rebate is rolling out, though millions of enrollees don't qualify. An NPR investigation reports ICE quietly ran a detention site out of a New Jersey warehouse this summer.

Abroad, the Middle East is the main risk to watch. Houthi rebels struck Saudi airports, killing three, after earlier attacks on Saudi oil sites that have pushed oil prices up. In Ukraine, a Russian strike on a public bus killed 30 as blackouts deepen in Kyiv, and rhetoric between NATO-aligned Europe and Russia keeps escalating. South Korea recalled its ambassador to Ukraine in a dispute over North Korean prisoners of war, and it test-flew its first homegrown hypersonic weapon after a North Korean hypersonic launch and mine blasts on the border. In France, student protests over school funding are drawing comparisons to May 1968, and Indonesia is restricting access to forest data as deforestation rises.

home.overview:
Baseball's final four is nearly set. The Dodgers closed out the Braves and will meet the Brewers in the NLCS, which eliminated the Padres, while the Rays swept the Yankees and await the winner of tonight's Game 4 between the White Sox (up 2–1) and Guardians. In the NFL, Thursday night features the winless Buccaneers at Dallas, with rookie QB Jalon Daniels starting for Tampa. The Chiefs, 49ers and Vikings are still unbeaten at 4–0, while Lamar Jackson and Ja'Marr Chase are uncertain for Sunday. The NBA season tips off Oct. 20, with Giannis Antetokounmpo starting his first year in Miami.

Club soccer returns this weekend after the international break, headlined by Liverpool vs. Man City on Sunday, with City perfect at 5–0 despite being found guilty on 114 Premier League charges, which the club is appealing. Barcelona are 7–0 in La Liga, and Dortmund lead the Bundesliga. In the break, England beat Croatia 7–0, the USA edged Canada 1–0 and South Korea beat Uzbekistan 2–0. In K League 1, FC Seoul lead by 15 points and host third-place Jeju on Saturday. The Champions League resumes Oct. 13–14.
